prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: complete opaque narrative setting plate for fantasy strategy game, C01-ARCH-SILVERWOOD, "Silverwood tree-city".
Primary request: redraw the first reference's exact forest tree-city identity in the approved broad matte chunky hand-painted cartoon style of the second and third references. Compose a new native 16:9 landscape image (target 1672x941 or a true 16:9 native canvas), not a square crop, with opaque painted scenery all the way to every edge.
Input roles: image 1 is the ORIGINAL SETTING AND ARCHITECTURAL CONTENT, its subject must survive; images 2 and 3 are approved STYLE references only. Do not import their rivers, stone towers, pine-dominated landscape, banners or military battle.
Scene: a secluded green tree-city built into three immense old broadleaf forest trunks. Thick golden-brown timber decks wrap around the living trunks at several levels, connected by gently curving rope-and-plank bridges with sturdy simple rails. A welcoming central small timber shrine/hall, moss-green curved roof, arched doorway, sits on the middle platform near the image center. Large roots reach the forest floor, and a winding earthen footpath comes forward between a few clustered garden beds. A few ladders link levels; a couple of modest hanging baskets and pulley baskets belong to this lived-in settlement. The distance is layered cool dark teal forest shade, with muted sun shafts and leafy canopy overhead. Preserve the original sense of enclosed forest depth and humane everyday life, not a monumental castle or futuristic elf capital.
People: a handful of small anonymous green-hooded forest residents/guards on the decks, with simple practical leather tunics and a few lowered spears or bows. No named heroes are being depicted. Keep them secondary to the architecture, no crowd.
Composition: three-quarter elevated isometric-like view consistent with the style references. Recompose the full multi-level city comfortably within the wide canvas; important platforms, bridges and roots are visible, not chopped off. The central hall, its platform, the central living trunk, and a recognizable connecting bridge must remain legible inside the middle 28 percent of image width so a narrow centered mobile cover still reads as a tree-city. Side trunks and peripheral foliage can extend beyond the edge, but keep major identity features clear with breathable spacing. Strong large silhouette clusters and a clear value hierarchy.
Style: match the approved fantasy cartoon scenes: confident charcoal-brown outlines, broad opaque matte color planes, chunky faceted warm wood, clean simplified forest green foliage clusters, restrained two- or three-step cel shading, sturdy toy-like small residents. Dramatically reduce the legacy image's hundreds of tiny leaves, scratch marks, hatching, woodgrain and speckles. Wood should read as a few large planks, foliage as large group shapes. Paint a beautiful finished scene, not flat vector art.
Lighting and palette: softly lit forest daytime; warm honey-brown timber, deep teal shadow, olive and moss-green leaves; enough separation that important wooden platforms and roots read clearly at 512x288 and 256x144. The center is slightly lighter than the side forest. Avoid murky crushed blacks or fluorescent green.
Text: none.
Constraints: preserve tree-city setting and source-era identity. No flags, no emblems, no written letters, no added dragon, no new humans, no battle, no burning or devastated forest, no magical crystal pylons. No decorative picture border, no white matte, no transparency, no checkerboard. No photorealism, plastic gloss, 3D rendering, airbrushed bloom or dense texture flecks. Deliver one coherent full-scene landscape, not a grid or collage.
